newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Indonesia seeks Jul/Aug mogas.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Indonesia seeks Jul/Aug mogas.

text.p: Singapore gasoline firmed on Monday on the back of stronger crude and Indonesian buying, traders said.
"Gasoline is balanced...directionally it should follow crude up," a trader, with a major oil company, said.
Talk in the Singapore market was thin but traders assessed the market as balanced amid Indonesian purchases to cover shortfalls during refinery turnarounds.
"Indonesia has been buying but quietly," a trader said.
Traders said any imports by Indonesia should prop up the lacklustre market.
"It should support the market as there is not much demand otherwise," said a trader. "But at the same time, there is not much on the supply side."
Naphtha in comparison, was bearish with ample supplies.
Traders said although the arbitrage window was now closed, a few prompt early August cargoes from the Mediterranean have not been placed.
Singapore naphtha swaps were steady despite the hike in crude prices with July quotes unchanged from Friday at $20.40/$20.50 per barrel.
